note: Placeholder bank written to unblock the architecture. Every question must be re-checked by hand against plan v2 sections 3.1 and 3.2 before client use. See docs/PENDING.md.

questions.framing: A week usually comes down to one or two moments with other people.
questions.question: Think of one recent interaction that stuck with you. What did you want from the other person, how did they respond, and what did you do next?

questions.framing: Being let down is specific; it happens at a moment, with a person.
questions.question: Think of the last time someone close let you down. What had you wanted from them, what did they do, and what did you do after?

questions.framing: Most people say less than they mean at least once a day.
questions.question: Think of one recent moment you held something back with someone. What did you want to say, and what did you say instead?

questions.framing: Wanting something from someone and not asking is common enough to have a shape.
questions.question: Think of a recent time you wanted something from someone close to you and did not ask. What was it, and what did you do instead?

questions.framing: A conversation you keep not having is still a conversation you're having with yourself.
questions.question: Think of a conversation you have been putting off. What do you expect the other person to say, and what would you do right after they said it?

questions.framing: The first sentence after a mistake is usually the one worth looking at.
questions.question: Think of a mistake from this week. What was the first sentence that went through your head, and what did you do in the next few minutes?

questions.framing: Talking yourself out of something takes an argument, and arguments have claims.
questions.question: Think of a recent moment when you talked yourself out of doing something. What exactly did you tell yourself, and how did you know it was true?

questions.framing: Some comments land harder than their size.
questions.question: Think of the most recent time a comment got under your skin. What was said, and what did you do in the minutes after?

questions.framing: Some of what we say to ourselves we would never say to anyone else.
questions.question: Think of one moment this week when you were hard on yourself. What was the exact wording in your head, and what had just happened?

questions.framing: The moment of putting something off is short and easy to miss.
questions.question: Pick one thing you put off this week. At the moment you would have started it, what did you do instead?

questions.framing: Everyone has something they reach for when a thought gets loud.
questions.question: What do you reach for when you want to stop thinking about something, and what were you thinking about the last time you reached for it?

questions.framing: A decision left open takes up room.
questions.question: Is there a choice you have been leaving open past when it needed making? What happened the last time you sat down to decide it?

questions.framing: Ordinary weeks have ordinary events in them, and those count.
questions.question: How did things go with friends this week? Give one example.

questions.framing: Work and school take most of the week, so they get a question.
questions.question: How did things go at work or school this week? Give one specific moment.

questions.framing: Sleep and routine shift before anything else does.
questions.question: What did your sleep and your mornings look like this week compared with last? Give one night or one morning.

questions.framing: Things we stop doing rarely announce themselves.
questions.question: Is there something you used to do regularly that you have not done lately? When was the last time, and what was going on that day?

questions.framing: Your word for a feeling is better than anyone else's.
questions.question: Pick one moment from this week that had a strong feeling in it. What is one word you would use for it, and what made it that word and not another?

questions.framing: Feelings show up in the body before they get a name.
questions.question: Think of a moment this week when you noticed something in your body before you knew what you felt. Where was it, and what was happening around you?

questions.framing: Wanting something different and wanting things to stay the same usually sit side by side.
questions.question: What, if anything, makes you want things to be different here, and what makes you want to leave them as they are?

questions.framing: Some wants stay unsaid for a long time.
questions.question: What is something you want that you have not said out loud, and what do you picture happening if you said it to one specific person?

questions.framing: Things that go well have causes too.
questions.question: What is one thing that went well this week, and what did you do that helped it go that way?

questions.framing: Small moments count here.
questions.question: When did you feel most like yourself this week? What were you doing, and who was there?

questions.framing: Asking for something and getting it is worth writing down.
questions.question: Was there a moment this week when you said what you needed and it worked out? What did you say, and what happened?
